rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhayli distinguishes على عيني, which evokes Moses being raised openly and safely after hidden danger, from بأعيننا, which means divine care and protection without an emphasis on disclosure.
rows.anchor: والفرق أن الآية الأولى وردت في إظهار أمر كان خفيا وإبداء ما كان مكنونا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular eye in Moses’ story signals a special intimacy, matching God’s statement that He chose Moses for Himself; the plural in the ark passages lacks this degree of exclusive favor.
rows.anchor: ولم يتكلم السهيلي على حكمة الإفراد في قصة موسى والجمع في الباقي

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhayli says nafs denotes the reality of existence without an additional sense; its relation to نفاسة and نفيس makes it suitable as a direct expression for God, unlike metaphorical terms discussed earlier.
rows.anchor: وأما النفس فعبارة عن حقيقة الوجود دون معنى زائد وقد استعمل من لفظها النفاسة

rows.speaker: أكثر الناس
rows.claim: Most people equate ذات with nafs, essence, and existence, and cite the report about Abraham’s three statements being في ذات الله as support.
rows.anchor: ويقولون ذات البارئ هي نفسه ويعبرون بها عن وجوده وحقيقته

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhayli rejects ذات as an expression for God’s essence: Arabic and religious usage instead mean His religion or law, as the phrase في ذات الله indicates.
rows.anchor: وليست هذه اللفظة إذا استقريتها في اللغة والشريعة كما زعموا

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: On the nominative reading of بل عجبت, Hamza and al-Kisa’i understand the wording to mean that the people have become objects of wonder.
rows.anchor: على قراءة حمزة والكسائي بضم التاء على معنى أنهم قد حلوا محل من يتعجب منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Noah’s story, نادى means that he was on the verge of calling; the following explanatory فـ would be absent if the call had already occurred. Zechariah’s قال directly explains his completed call without فـ.
rows.anchor: المراد قارب النداء لا أوقع النداء لدخول الفاء في فقال فإنه لو وقع النداء لسقطت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanatory فـ joins a specific explanation to a general statement, as in “he performed ablution, then washed his face”; Noah intended the call, and the phrasing treats it as approaching rather than accomplished.
rows.anchor: هذه الفاء تفسيريه لانها عطفت مفسرا على مجمل كقوله توضأ فغسل وجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coming of a people’s appointed term can mean its approach, which answers the familiar objection that an already arrived term cannot be advanced or delayed.
rows.anchor: المعنى قارب وبه يندفع المسؤال المشهور فيها إن عند مجيء الاجل لا يتصور تقديم ولا تأخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording about death’s arrival means when death is near, not after death has already occurred.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى ﴿ كتب عليكم إذا حضر أحدكم الموت ﴾ أي قارب حضور الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes seeing the punishment as nearing the sight of it; alternatively, they truly see a falling fragment but mistake it for a piled cloud, so the punishment still takes them by surprise.
rows.anchor: على حقيقتها وذلك على ان يكون يرونه فلا يظنونه عذابا

words: لو تركوا من خلفهم ذرية ضعافا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to fear for orphans addresses guardians who are close to leaving weak children behind; it must apply before death, since the dead are no longer addressed.
rows.anchor: أي وليخش الذين ان شارفوا ان يتركوا وإنما أول الترك بمشارفة الترك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A verb can describe intending its action: reciting, standing for prayer, decreeing, judging, conferring, or divorcing; Ibn عباس reads يهد الله as willing to guide, avoiding an identical condition and result.
rows.anchor: وقريب منه إطلاق الفعل وإرادة إرادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial of punishment is a single general statement, not a ruling asserted anew in every age; repeating mention of the blessing serves to show the breadth of mercy, not to boast of favor.
rows.anchor: ذكر عند ذكر النعمة لم يكن إشارة إلى الحكم في كل زمان تذكيرا بالنعمة

words: لَمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُۥ مِن قَبْلُ سَمِيًّۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author groups لم نجعل له من قبل سميا with Quranic statements about what God did not make, alongside examples framed with ما جعل; he says these patterns distinguish whether renewal of the stated matter is expected.
rows.anchor: في جميع مواضع ما حصل المذكور أمورا لا يتوقع تجددها

words: لَمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُۥ مِن قَبْلُ سَمِيًّۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zarkashi presents Quranic rhetorical styles as the book’s chief aim because they disclose the secrets of the Quran’s inimitable composition, arrangement, sweetness, and fluency.
rows.anchor: وهو المقصود الأعظم من هذا الكتاب وهو بيت القصيدة وأول الجريدة وغرة الكتيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An interpretation that compares the disbelievers to the Prophet depends on taking الناعق as a caller, but the author says that sense is not necessary.
rows.anchor: والذي أحوجه إلى هذا التقدير أنه لما شبه الذين كفروا بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author instead likens bewildered disbelievers to livestock hearing its herder call: they invoke things that cannot hear, see, or understand, with an ellipsis in the parable.
rows.anchor: بل الناعق من الحيوان شبههم في تألهم وتأتيهم بما ينعق من الغنم بصاحبه

rows.speaker: الصفار
rows.claim: Al-Saffar calls Sibawayh’s account weak: it requires extensive deletion from both coordinated clauses while leaving the conjunction, and the supposed link to the preceding words is absent.
rows.anchor: وقد قال الصفار هذا الذي صار إليه سيبويه من أنه حذف من الأول

rows.speaker: ابن الحجاج
rows.claim: Ibn al-Hajjaj sees no ellipsis: the disbelievers’ idol worship is a direct simile of a caller addressing something unable to hear; on this reading the disbelievers are callers, not the ones called.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الحجاج عندي أنه لا حذف في الآية والقصد تشبيه الكفار في عبادتهم لاصنام

words: أَفَمَن يَمْشِى مُكِبًّا عَلَىٰ وَجْهِهِۦٓ أَهْدَىٰٓ أَمَّن يَمْشِى سَوِيًّا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each half of the paired comparison omits what the other supplies; the comparative requires four elements, and the implicit answer is that the one walking upright on a straight path is more guided.
rows.anchor: فإن فيه جملتين حذف نصف كل واحدة منهما اكتفاء بنصف الآخرى وأصل الكلام أفمن يمشي مكبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The examples يحيي ويميت and Moses’ question about worshipping what neither hears nor sees omit objects because the point is God’s power to give life and death and the idol’s lack of senses.
rows.anchor: والمراد أن الله تعالى له الإحياء والإماتة وأن إلههم ليس له سمع ولا بصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Midian episode, objects are omitted from watering and fending verbs: the passage foregrounds the actions and encounter, while whether the animals were sheep, camels, or something else is beside its point.
rows.anchor: حذف منها المفعول خمس مرات لأنه غير مراد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the objects are omitted because the action, not the watered animals, is the point; Moses helped the women because they were fending while others watered, not because their animals were a particular kind.
rows.anchor: موافقة للزمخشري فإنه قال ترك المفعول لأن الغرض هو الفعل لا المفعول

rows.speaker: السكاكي
rows.claim: Al-Sakkaki classifies these omitted objects as deletion for concision even though the objects remain intended.
rows.anchor: وجعله السكاكي من الضرب الأول أعني مما حذف فيه للاختصار مع الإرادة

rows.speaker: الجزري
rows.claim: Al-Jazari prefers al-Sakkaki: the sheep matter because their weakness, combined with the women’s weakness, makes their need more deserving of compassion and help.
rows.anchor: فإن الغنم ليست ساقطة عن الاعتبار بالأصالة فإن فيها ضعفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zarkashi says al-Zamakhshari’s analysis is nearer, since the excerpt’s focus is the act of tending or watering rather than the object.
rows.anchor: والأقرب قول الزمخشري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In negation, من can either make an otherwise non-universal expression exhaustive, as in ما جاءني من رجل, or emphasize a noun already universal under negation, as in من أحد; the author says this differs from Sibawayh’s equivalence of the two uses.
rows.anchor: ولها في النفي معنيان أحدهما إن تكون للتنصيص على العموم

words: وما من إله إلا إله واحد
rows.speaker: الصفار
rows.claim: Al-Saffar says من is emphatic in both negative constructions, including ما جاءني من رجل; since it adds exhaustive force with أحد, he extends that force to رجل and prefers Sibawayh’s account.
rows.anchor: قال الصفار وهو الصحيح عندي وانها مؤكدة في الموضعين

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Abu Ja‘far ibn al-Zubayr says Sibawayh explicitly treats من as exhaustive: without it, ما أتاني رجل could deny only a strong man, only one man, or all men; with it, all three readings are denied.
rows.anchor: وقال الأستاذ أبو جعفر بن الزبير نص سيبويه على أنها نص في العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Interrogative constructions can take من in the same way as negation.
rows.anchor: ويلتحق بالنفي الاستفهام كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash allows زائد من in affirmative wording; here it means all sins, as confirmed by إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا, so the first verse is read with زائد من to avoid contradiction.
rows.anchor: وجوز الأخفش زيادتها في الاثبات

words: إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some fronting reflects the grammatical order of the sentence, such as an object preceding its subject in the cited examples.
rows.anchor: كتقديم المفعول على الفاعل في نحو قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting the object can convey restriction, as in asking whether anyone other than God is to be worshipped and declaring, “God alone I worship.”
rows.anchor: ونحوه مما يجب في الصناعة النحوية كذلك ولكن ذلك لقصد الحصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting the predicate مانعتهم before the subject حصونهم heightens the people’s confidence that their fortresses would protect them; ordinary order would not express that added confidence.
rows.anchor: ولو قال وظنوا أن حصونهم مانعتهم لما أشعر بزيادة وثوقهم بمنعها إياهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting راغب in أَرَاغِبٌ أَنتَ intensifies Abraham’s father’s denial; asking أأنت راغب عنها would not convey the same added disapproval.
rows.anchor: ما أفادت زيادة الإنكار على إبراهيم

words: فَإِذَا هِىَ شَٰخِصَةٌ أَبْصَٰرُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrasing فإذا هي شاخصة أبصار الذين كفروا retains the pronoun and marks disbelievers as the ones whose eyes are fixed; omitting هي would lose that particularizing force.
rows.anchor: وكان يستغنى عن الضمير لأن هذا لا يفيد اختصاص الذين كفروا بالشخوص

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi calls the account of the killing the story’s beginning, although it appears later in the recitation.
rows.anchor: قال البغوي هذا أول القصة وإن كانت مؤخرة في التلاوة

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi says the dispute preceded the cow’s slaughter; the command to slaughter made the audience understand its purpose was to reveal the hidden killer, so the later mention confirms what they already inferred.
rows.anchor: وقال الواحدي كان الاختلاف في القاتل قبل ذبح البقرة وإنما أخر في الكلام

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account treats this as wording placed later but intended earlier: the people disputed over a killing, asked Moses, and only then he told them that God commanded them to slaughter a cow.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنه من المؤخر الذي يراد به التقدم وتأويله

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zarkashi notes that al-Zamakhshari’s discussion indicates the Quran’s actual ordering yields a subtle rhetorical benefit, without detailing it here.
rows.anchor: وأما الزمخشري ففي كلامه ما يدل على أن إيرادها إنما كان يتأتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Throughout the Quran, حسبان means counting, except in al-Kahf 18:40, where it means punishment.
rows.anchor: وكل حرف فى القرآن حسبان فهو من العدد غير حرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حسرة usually means remorse; in آل عمران 3:156 it means grief.
rows.anchor: وكل ما فى القرآن حسرة فهو الندامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: دحض and داحض usually mean falsehood; المدحضين in al-Saffat is an exception with a different sense.
rows.anchor: وكل شىء فى القرآن الدحض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رجز means punishment throughout the Quran except in al-Muddaththir, where it means idols whose worship is to be abandoned.
rows.anchor: وكل حرف فى القرآن من رجز فهو العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ريب means doubt throughout the Quran except in the phrase ريب المنون, where it means the vicissitudes of time.
rows.anchor: وكل شىء فى القرآن من ريب فهو شك غير حرف واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forms of رجم generally mean killing, but Abraham’s father’s threat لأرجمنك means “I will insult you.”
rows.anchor: وكل شىء فى القرآن يرجمنكم و يرجموكم فهو القتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author adds that رجما بالغيب means conjecture, while rajm can also mean expulsion or cursing; رجيم is said of Satan for this reason.
rows.anchor: أى ظنا والرجم أيضا الطرد واللعن ومنه قيل للشيطان رجيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: زور ordinarily means falsehood and may denote associating partners with God; in al-Mujadila it means a lie without the sense of shirk.
rows.anchor: وكل شىء فى القرآن من زور فهو الكذب ويراد به الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: زكاة usually means wealth, but in the description of John it means tenderness or compassion.
rows.anchor: وكل شىء فى القرآن من زكاة فهو المال غير التى فى سورة مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: زاغوا and لا تزغ usually mean turning aside; when eyes زاغت in al-Ahzab, the meaning is that they stared fixedly.
rows.anchor: وكل شىء فى القرآن من زاغوا ولا تزغ فإنه من مالوا ولا تمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سخرون and سخرنا usually mean mockery; سخريا in al-Zukhruf instead means helpers or servants.
rows.anchor: وكل شىء فى القرآن من يسخرون وسخرنا فإنه يراد به الاستهزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سكينة normally means tranquility in the heart; in the Ark passage it is described as an object like a cat’s head with two wings.
rows.anchor: وكل سكينة فى القرآن طمأنينة فى القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Oath and condition may govern one another: whichever comes first supplies the answer, and the later element’s answer is omitted or subsumed.
rows.anchor: القسم والشرط يدخل كل منهما على الآخر فإن تقدم القسم ودخل الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In لئن لم تنته لأرجمنك, the first lām introduces the conditional clause and signals an expected oath answer; the lām in لأرجمنك marks that answer.
rows.anchor: تقديره والله لئن لم تنته فاللام الداخلة على الشرط ليس بلام القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer belongs to the oath, not the condition: it bears lām and is not jussive; the non-jussive response in the challenge that humans and jinn cannot match the Quran demonstrates the rule.
rows.anchor: والذي يدل على الجواب للقسم لا للشرط دخول اللام فيه وأنه ليس بمجزوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ولئن متم أو قتلتم لإلى الله تحشرون, the first lām is the oath signal and the second is the oath lām; the intervening prepositional phrase explains why the verb lacks emphatic nūn.
rows.anchor: والأصل لئن متم أو قتلتم لتحشرون إلى الله

words: وننزل من القرآن ما هو شفاء ورحمة للمؤمنين
rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri reportedly saw the Prophet in a dream while his son was gravely ill; the Prophet directed him to six healing verses, which he recited three times, after which his son recovered.
rows.anchor: ويحكى أن الشيخ أبا القاسم القشيري رأى النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم فى المنام

rows.speaker: ميمونة بنت شاقولة البغدادية
rows.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi recounts that Maimuna bint Shaqula prayed two rak‘as and recited one verse from the opening of each sura against a harmful neighbor; at dawn he fell and died.
rows.anchor: وحكى ابن الجوزى عن ابن ناصر عن شيوخه عن ميمونة بنت شاقولة البغدادية

words: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُمْسِكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ أَنْ تَزُولَا
rows.speaker: ابنها
rows.claim: Her son says she wrote a prayer invoking God’s holding the heavens and earth, placed it in a hollow wall, and instructed him to retrieve it after her death; it had remained there nearly twenty years.
rows.anchor: وحكى عن ابنها أنه كان فى دارها حائط له جوف فقالت هات رقعة ودواة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding position is approved by scholars because it avoids both anthropomorphism and negation; the Throne is uniquely eminent, the first creation, surrounded by angels, linked to the station of nearness, and the roof of Paradise.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول مرضي عند العلماء لسلامته من التشبيه والتعطيل وللعرش خصوصية ليست لغيره

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation takes نفسي here to mean rain, likened to the soul because it is hidden.
rows.anchor: قيل النفس هاهنا الغيث تشبيها له بالنفس لأنه مستتر كالنفس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation of يحذركم الله نفسه is “God warns you of His punishment”; another takes it as “God warns you of Himself.”
rows.anchor: أي عقوبته وقيل يحذركم الله إياه

words: وَهُوَ اللَّهُ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَفِي الْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: البيهقي
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqi, whom the author calls most correct, reads this as God being the one worshipped in heaven and earth, like the statement that He is a deity in each.
rows.anchor: اختار البيهقي معناه أنه المعبود في السماوات والأرض مثل قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: الأشعري
rows.claim: Al-Ash‘ari’s al-Mujiz reads the phrase as saying that God knows what is in the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: وقال الأشعري في ( الموجز )

rows.speaker: المجسمة
rows.claim: The Mujassima treat وهو الله في السماوات as a complete sentence and وفي الأرض يعلم as a separate clause.
rows.anchor: كلام آخر وهذا قول المجسمة

rows.speaker: الجهمية
rows.claim: The Jahmiyya use the verse to argue that God is in every place; the author calls this understanding among the most unsound interpretations.
rows.anchor: واستدلت الجهمية بهذه الآية على أنه تعالى في كل مكان وظاهر ما فهموه من الآية من أسخف الأقوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reads the wording as an idiomatic substitution of و for ب: the king comes with the army by his authority, just as the angel comes by God’s command; “go, you and your Lord” similarly means with His aid.
rows.anchor: قيل استعارة الواو موضع الباء لمناسبة بينهما في معنى الجمع إذ الباء موضوعة للإلصاق

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets عن ساق as referring to severe hardship.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة عن شدة وقال إبراهيم النخعي

rows.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
rows.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakha‘i interprets عن ساق as referring to a great event, supporting the sense with a line describing war rising to its ساق.
rows.anchor: وقال إبراهيم النخعي ( 3 ) أي عن أمر عظيم قال الشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran selects عمل for processes extended over time, such as making livestock, fruit, and crops, and فعل for swift acts such as angels obeying instantly or nations being destroyed.
rows.anchor: وقد اعتبره الله تعالى فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عملوا الصالحات suggests persistence in good works; افعلوا الخير means hasten to do good, as reinforced by فاستبقوا الخيرات and by prompt payment to meet the poor’s needs.
rows.anchor: حيث كان المقصود المثابرة عليها لا الإتيان بها مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He distinguishes قعود, which conveys remaining or stability, from جلوس, which does not require duration; he supports the difference through roots, usage, and the contrast between قعد and جلس forms.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك القعود والجلوس إن القعود لا يكون معه لبثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quranic قعود forms mark fixedness: positions for battle, staying with those who stay, and a permanent seat of truth; مجالس instead suits brief sitting, such as a gathering where people make room.
rows.anchor: فان الثبات هو المقصود وقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic says جليس الملوك rather than قعيد الملوك because royal company calls for brief, light sitting; قعيدة names a woman because she stays in her place.
rows.anchor: ولهذا لايقال قعيد الملوك وإنما يقال جليسهم
